provenance.author: block B1 writer (Claude Opus 5.5, model-written)
notes: Beat realised in four sections: the transformation and the discovery of fins, tails and scales (Hud!), the deep pool and the frightened small fish (Y llyn dwfn), the pike's claim 'Fy afon i yw hi!' and the chase in which Arth draws the pike away from Mali, and Myrddin's hand lifting them out ('Ydy e'n frenin da? Nac ydy. Mae'r pysgod yn ofni ei ddannedd e.'). End of Rhan 1: the Gramadeg carries the Rhan 1 cumulative mutation table.

Primary target G10: fy + NM (nwylo, nhraed, nannedd, ngwallt, nhrwyn, mhysgod; fy llyn / fy afon unchanged), dy + SM (draed, goesau, lygaid, geg, gefn, wallt, ddannedd), ei 'his' + SM (law, gorff, gefn, ben, gynffon, drwyn, geg, ddannedd), ei 'her' + AM six times (phen, chorff, chynffon ×2, cheg ×2). Contrasts: 'Does dim dwylo gyda ti' (G08) ↔ 'Ble mae fy nwylo i?'; 'Mae cynffon gyda fe' ↔ 'ei gynffon e'. ein / eich / eu each three times, receptive only, with echo pronouns.
Productive subset respected in Pensa: only fy and dy with body parts and ei (his) with p / t / c / d radicals are tested; ei (her) + AM is not tested.

Continuity with Pennod 11 (written in parallel): Myrddin's hat stayed in the kitchen; Dafi flies home alone at the end of Pennod 10; Cai rides home first; Myrddin, Arth, Mali and Pero walk home at nightfall.
Kingship thread planted as an action, not a moral: the pike rules by fear; Arth draws the pike away to save Mali; Myrddin answers Arth's question with silence and a smile.
The echo pronoun 'di' is added as a form of cy-ti in lexicon-deltas/pennod-10.json (it was not in the plan).

Applied gpt-6-astra review (2026-10-12): Rhan 1 mutation table now says feminine singular for the article, adjective and un rows, gives the ll-/rh- exceptions (yn llawn, y llaw, un llaw), excludes verb-nouns after yn, and names the imperative's direct object; Pensa A a1–a8 accept the forms without the echo pronoun, B b7 accepts brenin, B b8 accepts asgell, C c1/c2 accept further correct answers; '=' glosses that were associations (cuddio, Dyma fi) are now define glosses; cy-asgell sense now 'fin (of a fish); wing'; Mali's tail now 'o dan y garreg'; nodyn says the echo pronoun is optional.

Checker warnings left: lemma-validation for penhwyad (already in chapters.json validation.not_in_corcencc); media-manifest for the hand-authored SVG (media/manifest.json is not owned by this writer; integrator to add the entry); recall warnings for ein / eich / eu, cefn, corff, cen, dwfn, which depend on Penodau 11–15 (other writers).
SVG margin diagram cy-brenin-01-l10-img-corff.svg (boy ↔ fish, Welsh labels) is authored and on disk (status draft); the cover, scene and vignettes are planned raster art.

Continuity fix (2026-10-17): Dafi cannot really fly (Pennod 9 'dwyt ti ddim yn hedfan yn bell'; Pennod 16 'Adenydd bach … Bach iawn!'), so s150 now has him hop from Pero to the bridge and run home through the trees, instead of flying alone to the llys.

Audit-fix pass 2026-10-19 (docs/reviews/welsh-russian-lessons-2026-10-19.md): achub was used unglossed at s102 and glossed only at s114, with a false equation ('achub: codi o'r dŵr'). s102 is now 'Mae Arth yn gweld Mali, ac mae e'n ddewr.' (echoes Mali's s067; his rescue is shown by s103–s109), so achub first appears at s114 with the gloss 'achub: o geg y penhwyad', and Mali's s136 then names both rescues. Pensa: b7 accepted two bank words (penhwyad/brenin), now 'mae e'n dal ___ mawr, gwyrdd' → penhwyad only; b8 'mae ___ gyda fe' fitted ceg, trwyn, corff and cefn too, now cued by swimming (esgyll); b1 now uses the chapter's own 'ei ___ e' (→ geg) instead of 'agor y geg'; C c1–c3 accept 'Pysgod yw Arth a Mali', 'Penhwyad' and fuller answers.

cover.alt: Under the water: two small fish, Arth with a tuft-like fin and Mali with a dark stripe, face a huge green pike with open jaws full of sharp teeth; little fish hide under the stones.
cover.art_brief: Underwater, the dark pool under the old stone bridge on Afon Helyg (river greens, blue-black depths, sun shafts from above, the dark hull of an old rowing boat on the surface). Centre-left: Arth-fish, a small silver fish recognisable by a big untidy brown tuft-like fin sticking up on its back (Arth's cowlick) and a brave look; beside him Mali-fish, a slim fish with a long dark stripe down her back like her braid, wary. Facing them from the right, filling half the frame, the pike (penhwyad: a huge long green-and-gold river pike, pointed snout, underslung jaw full of needle-sharp white teeth, cold yellow eyes; menacing but storybook, never gory), jaws open. In the foreground small yellow, grey and silver fish hide under big stones and dead leaves. No text, no humans.

grammar.nodyn_en: Possessives precede the noun; an optional echo pronoun follows: fy nwylo i (my hands), dy draed di (your feet), ei geg e (his mouth), ei cheg hi (her mouth). Fy adds a nasal mutation, dy and ei 'his' a soft one, ei 'her' an aspirate one (c → ch, p → ph, t → th). Ein, eich, eu: recognition only.
